candidate.educational_objective: Coordinate interprofessional care through shared goals, clear roles, one communicated care plan, and direct client participation in decisions.

options.A: Coordinate the disciplines around one shared care plan, clarify roles and goals, and include the client directly in discussions and decisions about the plan.
options.B: Ask each discipline to create an independent plan without discussing priorities with the others because separate professional judgment reduces interdisciplinary conflict.
options.C: Assign one discipline to determine every aspect of treatment and ask the other disciplines to follow that plan even when their assessments identify different needs.
options.D: Exclude the client from team planning until professionals reach agreement because patient preferences should be considered only after the interdisciplinary plan is finalized.

candidate.rationale: AHRQ TeamSTEPPS states that the patient care team is not complete without the patient and that patients collaborate in creating the care plan. Team leadership tools emphasize defining clear goals, roles, expected outcomes, and a shared care plan. A coordinated interdisciplinary plan that includes the client is therefore the best response.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Effective team leadership coordinates a shared patient care plan with clear goals/roles and includes the patient as a member of the care team.
